hook.text: A vinyl record stores sound as a continuous groove. A CD stores it as billions of discrete ones and zeros.

buildup.text: Analog signals are continuous—infinite values at infinite time points. Digital signals are discrete steps.

discovery.text: Digital signals can be copied perfectly. Analog signals degrade with every copy as noise accumulates.

twist.text: Digitization loses information—rounding continuous values to steps. But the tradeoff is near-perfect reliability.

climax.text: The digital revolution happened because discrete signals resist noise. Error correction is possible, perfection isn't.

punchline.text: Continuous is natural. Discrete is reliable.

quiz.question: Why did digital signals replace analog in most systems?
options: They resist noise and can be copied perfectly
